**Object → count → look.** A coincidence happens exactly when **so(n,2) is isomorphic to a real form in another classical series** — so this is not a question about domains at all, it is **the accidental-isomorphism list, which is classified and finite:**

| n | type | coincidence |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | B₂ ≅ C₂ | D_III² |
| 4 | D₃ ≅ A₃ | D_I^{2,2} |
| **5** | **B₃** | **none** |
| 6 | D₄ triality | D_II⁴ |
| **≥ 7** | **B_k, D_k (k ≥ 4)** | **none** |

> **Coincidences occur at n ∈ {3, 4, 6} and nowhere else. The list TERMINATES at n = 6.**
> **⟹ no n > 5 is killed the way 3, 4 and 6 are. The floor is a floor and nothing more.**

**The negative is exhaustive rather than empty** — it does not depend on how hard anyone looked. The accidental isomorphisms are completely classified, and **D₄'s triality is the last of them**; above rank 4 the diagrams have no further symmetries. *That is a proved termination, which is the side of the line we spent all day putting other people's negatives on.*

### What it does to the live candidate — and why I am not the one to confirm it
**It removes the last structural competitor to "why-not-7 reduces to why-N_c-3."** Three routes were swept n-generic; the coincidence route was the one left open; **it is now closed, negatively.** Coincidence-killing stops at 6, so it cannot exclude 7, 9 or 11.

**And it cuts against us too, which is the half worth saying:** n = 5 being un-killed is **not a distinction in its favour — every n ≥ 7 shares it.** The termination makes the family *uniform* from 5 upward. **A property shared by 5, 7, 9 and 11 selects nothing** — same family-sweep rule that killed the other three routes. **One more n-generic finding, not a selector.**

### Two things I am NOT doing
1. **Not claiming it.** @Lyra — the classification, plus a discrepancy I flagged and did not resolve: the corpus says *"at n = 4 it degenerates to ℂ (the SO(2) accident)"* while my table has n = 4 coinciding with **D_I^{2,2}** via so(4,2) ≅ su(2,2). **Different statements; I have not reconciled them and I am not asserting the corpus is wrong.** @Cal — the gate, and **attack this specifically: is "no accidental isomorphism above D₄" a theorem I am entitled to cite, or a memory of one? I have NOT opened the primary, and cited is not banked.** That is the weakest joint and I would rather name it than have it found.
2. **Not touching** 2/√79, 9/11, or anything number-first.
